title: United States 2-0 Haiti (8-0 agg): Pochettino signs off in style
subtitle: Mauricio Pochettino will head into his stint in charge of Manchester United on the back of a routine win in his final United States match.
paragraphs: Christian Pulisic and Julian Hall scored the final goals of Mauricio Pochettino's tenure as the United States dispatched Haiti 2-0 to seal an 8-0 aggregate win.
The USA were all but sure of their place in the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals prior to Tuesday's contest, given they led 6-0 from the first leg.
And there was no drama at TQL Stadium as first-half goals from Pulisic and Hall ensured Pochettino signed off with a routine win.
Pochettino will now head off to join Manchester United, having been appointed as the Red Devils' new head coach.
Pulisic provided the standout moment in Cincinnati, opening the scoring in the 25th minute with an exceptional overhead kick.
Teenager Hall continued his remarkable run of form, netting his fifth goal in the space of six caps just before half-time.
Hall took his goal in composed fashion, creating space in the area and slotting home under pressure.
The USA have now won their last six games and have not conceded since September 29, as Pochettino heads off to Old Trafford in style.

While it did not match the standard of Saturday's romp, this was an accomplished, dominant display from the Stars and Stripes, who conceded just two shots on target and created chances worth a combined 1.43 expected goals to Haiti's 0.85 xG.
The USA have extended their unbeaten run against Haiti across all competitions (including friendlies) to 12 matches, winning each of the last five (W7 D5 since 1976).
Pochettino may be going, but whoever comes in as the USMNT's next boss has plenty of quality at their disposal.
Pulisic is the USA's leading goalscorer in the CONCACAF Nations League, having found the net nine times – at least two more than any other teammate.
Weston McKennie, who assisted both goals here, is the next closest, with seven, alongside Ricardo Pepi.
But Hall continues to show immense potential. At 18 years and 238 days old, he is the youngest player ever to reach five goals for the USMNT, surpassing Pulisic (18 years and 258 days).
html:
Christian Pulisic and Julian Hall scored the final goals of Mauricio Pochettino's tenure as the United States dispatched Haiti 2-0 to seal an 8-0 aggregate win.

The USA were all but sure of their place in the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals prior to Tuesday's contest, given they led 6-0 from the first leg.

And there was no drama at TQL Stadium as first-half goals from Pulisic and Hall ensured Pochettino signed off with a routine win.

Pochettino will now head off to join Manchester United, having been appointed as the Red Devils' new head coach.

Pulisic provided the standout moment in Cincinnati, opening the scoring in the 25th minute with an exceptional overhead kick.

Teenager Hall continued his remarkable run of form, netting his fifth goal in the space of six caps just before half-time.

Hall took his goal in composed fashion, creating space in the area and slotting home under pressure.

The USA have now won their last six games and have not conceded since September 29, as Pochettino heads off to Old Trafford in style.

The future's bright

While it did not match the standard of Saturday's romp, this was an accomplished, dominant display from the Stars and Stripes, who conceded just two shots on target and created chances worth a combined 1.43 expected goals to Haiti's 0.85 xG.

The USA have extended their unbeaten run against Haiti across all competitions (including friendlies) to 12 matches, winning each of the last five (W7 D5 since 1976).

Pochettino may be going, but whoever comes in as the USMNT's next boss has plenty of quality at their disposal.

Pulisic is the USA's leading goalscorer in the CONCACAF Nations League, having found the net nine times – at least two more than any other teammate.

Weston McKennie, who assisted both goals here, is the next closest, with seven, alongside Ricardo Pepi.

But Hall continues to show immense potential. At 18 years and 238 days old, he is the youngest player ever to reach five goals for the USMNT, surpassing Pulisic (18 years and 258 days).
